chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Hearing Tatum at a 136th Street party
summary: He stuck his foot in the door of a party and heard "Tea for Two" sounding like two pianos.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: So I heard about him, but... One night, I was walking on Seventh Avenue, and on 136th Street they were having a party, a birthday party...whichever... Either it was a house rent party or a birthday party, whichever it was. And I heard this piano coming from outside the window. Somebody said, "Listen, that's Art Tatum playing in there." Then the name struck me, you know. I went over on 136th Street, and it was on the ground floor. So the person said, "What do you want?" And I stuck my foot in the door, which was a real Harlem...! "Get your foot outta the door." I had some of my buddies. I was local, you know. "Well, I want to come in." He said, "Well, you can't come in." "What do you mean, I can't come in. Hey, Harry! Oh yes, we're coming in to hear the piano player." So there's nothing the guy could do. He gave up the door.

Everybody was dancing. So I looked around at the people. The couples were dancing. And I saw the keys coming up, but I didn't see the hands! I saw the keys coming up. Like, he had made an impression... He was so fast that the keys were still trembling. You know, they were (?)! So I heard "Tea For Two," and it sounded like two pianos, you know. I looked for the other piano; it wasn't there.

So I left the room, and I saw this guy hunched over the piano, and he had little hands, and his hands were going over the keys... As Percy Lee later described it, "his hands looked like mice going over the piano." He wasn't musically oriented, you know...
Percy Lee. He was a fellow that owned one of the hideaways, you know. Anyway, that stuck in my mind. I thought it was great.

Anyway, I said, "What is your name" -- he was playing. He said, "Tatum, Tatum. Art Tatum." I said, "Yeah?" And he was hunching over... And I just watched those hands. It was unbelievable. I just couldn't believe that one piano...you know, it sounded like that. He used to play the (?) on the left hand...
